#### **Results of Operations**

Tesla 2024 10-K
#### **Revenues**

In the year 2024, Tesla's automotive sales revenues were $72,480 million. Compared to 2023, this represented a decrease of $6,029 million, or 8%. In contrast, automotive sales revenues increased by $11,299 million, or 17%, from 2022 to 2023, when the revenues were $67,210 million and $78,509 million, respectively.

In 2024, Tesla's automotive regulatory credits were $2,763 million. This was an increase of $973 million, or 54%, compared to 2023, when the credits were $1,790 million. From 2022 to 2023, the credits increased by $14 million, or 1%, from $1,776 million.

Tesla's automotive leasing revenues were $1,827 million in 2024. This represented a decrease of $293 million, or 14%, compared to 2023, when the revenues were $2,120 million. From 2022 to 2023, the revenues decreased by $356 million, or 14%, from $2,476 million.

The total automotive revenues for Tesla in 2024 were $77,070 million. This was a decrease of $5,349 million, or 6%, compared to 2023, when the total automotive revenues were $82,419 million. In contrast, the total automotive revenues increased by $10,957 million, or 15%, from 2022 to 2023, when the revenues were $71,462 million.

In 2024, Tesla's revenues from services and other sources were $10,534 million. This represented an increase of $2,215 million, or 27%, compared to 2023, when the revenues were $8,319 million. From 2022 to 2023, the revenues increased by $2,228 million, or 37%, from $6,091 million.

The total revenues for Tesla's automotive and services and other segment in 2024 were $87,604 million. This was a decrease of $3,134 million, or 3%, compared to 2023, when the total revenues were $90,738 million. In contrast, the total revenues increased by $13,185 million, or 17%, from 2022 to 2023, when the revenues were $77,553 million.

Tesla's energy generation and storage segment revenue in 2024 was $10,086 million. This represented an increase of $4,051 million, or 67%, compared to 2023, when the revenue was $6,035 million. From 2022 to 2023, the revenue increased by $2,126 million, or 54%, from $3,909 million.

The total revenues for Tesla in 2024 were $97,690 million. This represented an increase of $917 million, or 1%, compared to 2023, when the total revenues were $96,773 million. In contrast, the total revenues increased by $15,311 million, or 19%, from 2022 to 2023, when the revenues were $81,462 million.

Tesla 2024 10-K
#### Automotive & Services and Other Segment

Tesla 2024 10-K
Automotive sales revenue includes revenues related to cash and financing deliveries of new vehicles, including access to our FSD (Supervised) features and their ongoing maintenance, internet connectivity, free Supercharging programs and over-the-air software updates. These deliveries are vehicles that are not subject to lease accounting.

Tesla 2024 10-K
Automotive regulatory credits includes sales of regulatory credits to other automotive manufacturers. Our revenue from automotive regulatory credits is directly related to our new vehicle production, sales and pricing negotiated with our customers. We monetize them proactively as new vehicles are sold based on standing arrangements with buyers of such credits, typically as close as possible to the production and delivery of the vehicle or changes in regulation impacting the credits.

Tesla 2024 10-K
Automotive leasing revenue includes the amortization of revenue for vehicles under direct operating lease agreements. Additionally, automotive leasing revenue includes direct sales-type leasing programs where we recognize all revenue associated with the sales-type lease upon delivery to the customer.

Tesla 2024 10-K
Services and other revenue consists of sales of used vehicles, non-warranty maintenance services and collision, part sales, paid Supercharging, insurance services revenue and retail merchandise sales.

Tesla 2024 10-K
#### <u>2024 compared to 2023</u>

Tesla 2024 10-K
Automotive sales revenue decreased $6.03 billion, or 8%, in the year ended December 31, 2024 as compared to the year ended December 31, 2023, primarily due to lower average selling price on our vehicles driven by overall price reductions and attractive financing options provided in 2024 as well as mix. Additionally, there was a decrease of approximately 22,000 combined Model 3 and Model Y cash deliveries. The decreases were partially offset by an increase of approximately 19,000 deliveries of

Tesla 2024 10-K
an increase of approximately 19,000 deliveries of other models primarily due to our production ramp of Cybertruck. Additionally, we recognized $596 million of FSD (Supervised) revenue due to release of certain features in 2024.

Tesla 2024 10-K
Automotive regulatory credits revenue increased $973 million, or 54%, in the year ended December 31, 2024 as compared to the year ended December 31, 2023, driven by demand for credits in North America as other automobile manufacturers scale back on their battery electric vehicle plans.

Tesla 2024 10-K
Automotive leasing revenue decreased $293 million, or 14%, in the year ended December 31, 2024 as compared to the year ended December 31, 2023, primarily due to lower direct sales-type leasing deliveries as we have shifted towards providing leasing options through commercial banking partner programs that allow for us to recognize upfront revenue in automotive sales and a decrease in lease buyouts.

Tesla 2024 10-K
Services and other revenue increased $2.22 billion, or 27%, in the year ended December 31, 2024 as compared to the year ended December 31, 2023, primarily due to increases in sales of used vehicles, non-warranty maintenance services and collision revenue, paid Supercharging revenue, insurance services revenue and part sales revenue.

Tesla 2024 10-K
#### Energy Generation and Storage Segment

Tesla 2024 10-K
Energy generation and storage revenue includes sales and leasing of solar energy generation and energy storage products, financing of solar energy generation products, services related to such products and sales of solar energy systems incentives.

Tesla 2024 10-K
#### <u>2024 compared to 2023</u>

Tesla 2024 10-K
Energy generation and storage revenue increased $4.05 billion, or 67%, in the year ended December 31, 2024 as compared to the year ended December 31, 2023, primarily due to a 16.7 GWh increase in Megapack and Powerwall deployments compared to the prior year.

Tesla 2024 10-K
#### **Cost of Revenues and Gross Margin**

In the year 2024, the cost of revenues for automotive sales was $61,870 million, which is a decrease of $3,251 million, or 5%, from the $65,121 million in 2023, and an increase of $15,522 million, or 31%, from the $49,599 million in 2022. 
In 2024, the cost of revenues for automotive leasing was $1,003 million, which is a decrease of $265 million, or 21%, from the $1,268 million in 2023, and a decrease of $241 million, or 16%, from the $1,509 million in 2022. 
The total automotive cost of revenues for 2024 was $62,873 million, which is a decrease of $3,516 million, or 5%, from the $66,389 million in 2023, and an increase of $15,281 million, or 30%, from the $51,108 million in 2022. 
The cost of revenues for services and other in 2024 was $9,921 million, which is an increase of $2,091 million, or 27%, from the $7,830 million in 2023, and an increase of $1,950 million, or 33%, from the $5,880 million in 2022. 
The total automotive and services and other segment cost of revenues for 2024 was $72,794 million, which is a decrease of $1,425 million, or 2%, from the $74,219 million in 2023, and an increase of $17,231 million, or 30%, from the $56,988 million in 2022. 
In 2024, the cost of revenues for the energy generation and storage segment was $7,446 million, which is an increase of $2,552 million, or 52%, from the $4,894 million in 2023, and an increase of $1,273 million, or 35%, from the $3,621 million in 2022. 
The total cost of revenues for 2024 was $80,240 million, which is an increase of $1,127 million, or 1%, from the $79,113 million in 2023, and an increase of $18,504 million, or 31%, from the $60,609 million in 2022. 
The gross profit for the total automotive segment in 2024 was $14,197 million, in 2023 was $16,030 million, and in 2022 was $20,354 million. 
The gross margin for the total automotive segment was 18.4% in 2024, 19.4% in 2023, and 28.5% in 2022. 
The gross profit for the total automotive and services and other segment in 2024 was $14,810 million, in 2023 was $16,519 million, and in 2022 was $20,565 million. 
The gross margin for the total automotive and services and other segment was 16.9% in 2024, 18.2% in 2023, and 26.5% in 2022. 
The gross profit for the energy generation and storage segment in 2024 was $2,640 million, in 2023 was $1,141 million, and in 2022 was $288 million. 
The gross margin for the energy generation and storage segment was 26.2% in 2024, 18.9% in 2023, and 7.4% in 2022. 
The total gross profit in 2024 was $17,450 million, in 2023 was $17,660 million, and in 2022 was $20,853 million. 
The total gross margin was 17.9% in 2024, 18.2% in 2023, and 25.6% in 2022.

Tesla 2024 10-K
Gross margin for energy generation and storage increased from 18.9% to 26.2% in the year ended December 31, 2024 as compared to the year ended December 31, 2023, primarily due to margin improvements for our energy storage products driven by cost reductions, including benefits from IRA manufacturing credits, and a higher proportion of our storage business, which operated at a higher gross margin, within the segment as compared to the prior periods.

Tesla 2024 10-K
#### **Research and Development Expense**

Research and development expense for the year ended December 31, 2024 was $4,540 million. 
In 2024, research and development expense as a percentage of revenues was 5%. 
Research and development expense for the year ended December 31, 2023 was $3,969 million. 
In 2023, research and development expense as a percentage of revenues was 4%. 
Research and development expense for the year ended December 31, 2022 was $3,075 million. 
In 2022, research and development expense as a percentage of revenues was 4%. 
The change in research and development expense from 2023 to 2024 was $571 million, which represents a 14% increase. 
The change in research and development expense from 2022 to 2023 was $894 million, which represents a 29% increase.

Tesla 2024 10-K
Research and development (“R&D”) expenses consist primarily of personnel costs for our teams in engineering and research, manufacturing engineering and manufacturing test organizations, prototyping expense, contract and professional services and amortized equipment expense.

Tesla 2024 10-K
R&D expenses increased $571 million, or 14%, in the year ended December 31, 2024 as compared to the year ended December 31, 2023. The overall increases were primarily driven by additional costs year over year related to AI programs. R&D expenses as a percentage of revenue increased from 4% to 5% in the year ended December 31, 2024 as compared to the year ended December 31, 2023 as we continue to expand our product roadmap and technologies.

Tesla 2024 10-K
#### **Selling, General and Administrative Expense**

In 2024, the selling, general and administrative expense was $5,150 million. 
In 2023, the selling, general and administrative expense was $4,800 million. 
In 2022, the selling, general and administrative expense was $3,946 million. 
From 2023 to 2024, the selling, general and administrative expense increased by $350 million, which represents a 7% change. 
From 2022 to 2023, the selling, general and administrative expense increased by $854 million, which represents a 22% change. 
In 2024, the selling, general and administrative expense was 5% of revenues. 
In 2023, the selling, general and administrative expense was 5% of revenues. 
In 2022, the selling, general and administrative expense was 5% of revenues.

Tesla 2024 10-K
Selling, general and administrative (“SG&A”) expenses generally consist of personnel and facilities costs related to our stores, marketing, sales, executive, finance, human resources, information technology and legal organizations, as well as fees for professional and contract services and litigation settlements.

Tesla 2024 10-K
SG&A expenses increased $350 million, or 7%, in the year ended December 31, 2024 as compared to the year ended December 31, 2023 driven by a $171 million increase in facilities related expenses, a $115 million increase in employee and labor costs, including professional services and a $57 million increase in marketing expenses.

Tesla 2024 10-K
#### **Restructuring and Other**

In 2024, the restructuring and other amount was $684 million. In 2023, the restructuring and other amount was $0 million, representing a $684 million and not meaningful percentage change from 2023. In 2022, the restructuring and other amount was $176 million, representing a $176 million and 100% decrease from 2022 to 2023.

Tesla 2024 10-K
In the second quarter of 2024, we initiated and substantially completed certain restructuring actions to reduce costs and improve efficiency. As a result, we recognized $583 million of employee termination expenses in Restructuring and other in our consolidated income statement. These expenses were substantially paid with an immaterial accrual remaining in Accrued liabilities and other in our consolidated balance sheet as of December 31, 2024.

#### **Interest Income**

In 2024, Tesla's interest income was $1,569 million. In 2023, Tesla's interest income was $1,066 million. In 2022, Tesla's interest income was $297 million. From 2023 to 2024, Tesla's interest income increased by $503 million, which represents a 47% change. From 2022 to 2023, Tesla's interest income increased by $769 million, which represents a 259% change.

Tesla 2024 10-K
Interest income increased $503 million, or 47%, in the year ended December 31, 2024 as compared to the year ended December 31, 2023, primarily due to higher interest earned on our cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments compared to the prior year due to an increase in our portfolio balance and a higher weighted average interest rate.

#### **Liquidity and Capital Resources**

Tesla 2024 10-K
We expect to continue to generate net positive operating cash flow. The cash we generate from our core operations enables us to fund ongoing operations and production, our research and development projects for new products and technologies including our proprietary battery cells, additional manufacturing ramps at existing manufacturing facilities, the construction of future factories, and the continued expansion of our retail and service locations, body shops, Mobile Service fleet, Supercharger,

Tesla 2024 10-K
body shops, Mobile Service fleet, Supercharger, including to support NACS, energy product installation capabilities and autonomy and other artificial intelligence enabled products.

Tesla 2024 10-K
In addition, because a large portion of our future expenditures will be to fund our growth, we expect that if needed we will be able to adjust our capital and operating expenditures by operating segment. For example, if our near-term manufacturing operations decrease in scale or ramp more slowly than expected, including due to global economic or business conditions, we may choose to correspondingly slow the pace of our capital expenditures. Finally, we continually evaluate our cash needs and may

Tesla 2024 10-K
